entities.summary: Hernando de Aragón y Gurrea, OCist, Archbishop of Zaragoza and Lieutenant General of Aragon, was an Aragonese humanist and historian. Born into a noble family, he studied at the University of Salamanca and later became a prominent figure in the Aragonese court. As Archbishop of Zaragoza, he played a key role in promoting the arts and humanities, establishing the Casa de la Cultura, and encouraging the translation of classical works into Catalan. His historical writings, including the 'Chronica de los Reys de Aragón', remain an important source of information on the history of the Crown of Aragon. De Aragón y Gurrea's legacy can be seen in the continued development of humanism and the arts in Aragon, as well as his influence on later historians and scholars. The 'Chronica' was translated into French in 1598, and its impact on European historiography was significant. De Aragón y Gurrea's commitment to education and the arts helped shape the cultural landscape of Aragon, leaving a lasting impact on the region's development. Through his writings, de Aragón y Gurrea ensured the survival of Aragonese cultural heritage, providing a window into the history of the Crown of Aragon and its people.

entities.name: Hernando de Aragón y Gurrea
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Hernando de Aragón y Gurrea, a grandson of the Catholic Monarchs Ferdinand II of Aragon and Isabella I of Castile, served as a pivotal figure in 16th-century Aragon, concurrently holding the influential positions of Archbishop of Zaragoza (1539–1575) and Lieutenant General of Aragon (1539–1566). Born on August 3, 1498, in Zaragoza, his royal lineage and intellectual acumen placed him at the nexus of ecclesiastical authority, political governance, and humanist scholarship during a transformative period for the Spanish monarchy and the Aragonese Crown. His enduring significance lies in his successful navigation of regional autonomy (fueros) with royal centralizing efforts, coupled with his profound contributions to Aragonese cultural identity.

Throughout his lengthy tenure, Hernando de Aragón was a prodigious patron of the arts and architecture, leaving an indelible mark on Zaragoza's urban and religious landscape. He initiated significant renovations and expansions of the Seo of Zaragoza (Cathedral of the Savior), including the construction of its Renaissance-style main altarpiece and the Chapel of San Bernardo, where he would later be interred. Beyond his architectural patronage, he meticulously reorganized the archives of La Seo and the Royal Archive of Aragon. As a historian, his most notable work, "Historia de Aragón" (History of Aragon), though unfinished and published posthumously, provided a crucial narrative of the kingdom's past, drawing heavily on primary sources and reflecting a keen humanist sensibility. He also played a key role in implementing the decrees of the Council of Trent within his archdiocese, reforming ecclesiastical practices and institutions.
